One thing you might have heard of, or consider using is the Pareito Principle. Basically, it means that 20% of your causes create 80% of your effects.

For example, Customers are Causes and Profits are Effects. According to this principle, you could expect to find that 20% of your customers generate 80% of your Profits. Equally, 20% of your Customers might create 80% of your headaches. This can extend into all areas of business, and life elsewhere. Look at search engine traffic, as another example, 20% of the search engines get 80% of the queries.

What tends to happen is that, the law of diminishing returns kicks in noticeably, if you keep going after you reach 80%. If you are cleaning something, it takes time. Lets say you have 100 meters to clean. You can clean the 1st 80 meters in 20 minutes. (You can get it 80% clean quickly.) But to get it 100% clean, it is going to take you a further 80 minutes! That is a huge increase in effort, for not so much improvement. Lets say that 20 meters was particularly grimy, due to an oil spill or something.

So, lets look at it again. There is a total of 100 Meters to clean. You do 80 meters quickly, and are left looking at the difficult remainder: 20 meters. How does that pan out? Well, once again, within that remaining 20 meters, the Pareito principle kicks in again! You can clean 80% of it in 20% of the time you give it. (80/100)*20=16 It would take 16 minutes to do the easiest 80% of the remainder, a further 16 meters. And so forth.
